**Tier 8.** Its `application`, `domain` and
`infrastructure` may import only a strictly lower tier. `http/` composes freely
but may never reach into another module's `http/` or `infrastructure/`.

May import: `account`, `activity`, `auth`, `cart`, `catalog`, `chat`, `commerce`, `contact`, `customers`, `delivery`, `identity`, `invoicing`, `loyalty`, `messaging`, `payments`, `plugins`, `seo`, `settings`, `shipping`, `vintedReviews`, `vouchers`.

Currently imports: `catalog`, `commerce`, `customers`, `delivery`, `identity`, `invoicing`, `messaging`, `payments`, `plugins`, `shipping`.

Feature map entry: `orders` in [docs/features.json](../../../docs/features.json). Run `npm run feature -- orders` for its full span.

## Invariants

<!-- invariants:start -->

Order records are immutable once placed. Totals, addresses, courier and item
snapshots are written at confirmation and never recomputed from live catalogue
data afterwards: a later price or product change must not alter what a customer
was charged. Address corrections go through the revision flow, which records
the change rather than overwriting the snapshot.

Status moves forward only, through `nextOrderStatus` in `domain/orderStatus.ts`.
Only `confirmed`, `in_preparation` and `to_send` are cancellable, because
cancelling after that would mean refunding captured funds.

**Never automatically refund a captured payment, and never treat a captured
PaymentIntent as cancellable.** Releasing an authorization before capture uses
the documented idempotent path. No cron, webhook or retry may decide a refund.

Confirmation must be idempotent: a webhook can arrive twice for the same
PaymentIntent, and the second arrival must not create a second order.

<!-- invariants:end -->
